notes.title: Patch/Update to the Playtest
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone,[/p][p][/p][p]I hope you have all been enjoying the playtest thus far. Further testing and development uncovered several major issues in the current game's build, particularly in relation to connecting to a match hosted by another. The latest update patches these issues. In the meantime, feel free to test out the new features that have been in the works.[/p][p][/p][h3]List of changes[/h3][list][*][p]Each vehicle now has an alternate choice of boost and powerup. Alternate boosts last longer but have longer charge-ups, and alternate powerups give each vehicle a unique twist based upon each vehicle's characteristics. Alternate powerups will likely require an unlock via achievement in the final game, but all are available immediately under the current test version.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a map: "Greenfield Village (Night)." This map is identical to Greenfield Village but is fought in a nighttime environment, with each vehicle given a set of lights to navigate it. Lights can be toggled on or off by pressing the "F" key under night rules.[/p][/*][*][p]Added the ability to adjust the skin of each vehicle. A camouflage pattern has been added, along with the ability to adjust each skin's coloration. The option to use a custom skin from the game's files (experimental) has also been added.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the error where a client occasionally failed to connect to another host.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the error where re-opening the "Join Lobby" screen froze the main menu when another's lobby was present.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the error where the fire effect from the boost was not present from anyone's vehicle except their own.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the error where a newly created lobby did not always receive a name.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the error where a client connected to another host occasionally had health bars and map icons display incorrectly.[/p][/*][*][p]Made other changes and improvements.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Known Issues[/h3][list][*][p]Some UI elements may display incorrectly.[/p][/*][*][p]Hit markers on vehicles project onto very nearby objects.[/p][/*][*][p]On rare occasions, a match may fail to start.[/p][/*][*][p]Transferring large or numerous custom skins may cause network issues early in a match.[/p][/*][*][p]A small hole in the Wagon XII's frontal hull armor appears to be present in the reticle, but this weak point does not actually exist.[/p][/*][*][p]The game is not optimized and requires more CPU and network strength than it appears.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Second Playtest is Live
notes.notes:
Good evening everyone,

The second playtest for [i]Steel Skirmish Reloaded: Online Multiplayer Tank Shooter[/i] is now live. I once again apologize for the wait for this release; motivation has been difficult to come by in the last few months. I would like to thank everyone for the feedback and support that has been given thus far, as your input is critical to the development of this project.

This test of the game is once again primarily a concept-based test, as I need to solidify the gameplay and basic features of the game before I can concentrate on creating content. Many changes and fixes have been made as opposed to the initial playtest, along with a small amount of new content. Here is the list of changes:

[h3]Return to P2P[/h3]
It was always my dream to run [i]Steel Skirmish Reloaded[/i] on dedicated servers, with random matchmaking and a competitive-style setup. The first playtest was run on dedicated hardware; however, the solution ultimately proved neither practical nor economical.

As a result, the second playtest uses a peer-to-peer relay model, very similar to the one used in the original [i]Steel Skirmish[/i]. The logic for each match is run on a participant's PC (the host), and the other players connect to it via a relay server that secures and streamlines the network traffic. This solution provides for straightforward gameplay and custom matchmaking; however, it does have the downside of being reliant on the host and having more lag than a dedicated server setup. If you play a match with another as the host, please be sure to let me know how the experience is.

[h3]Netcode Improvements[/h3]
The second playtest features improved netcode, meaning that remote gameplay is smoother and easier to play on. For those not playing as a host, vehicle movement is much smoother, and a server rewind system was used for shots to make firing feel more instantaneous. These changes should make the game significantly more comfortable to play, especially for those with a weaker network.

[h3]Gameplay Adjustments[/h3]
The first test felt a bit too rushed after reconsideration, so the decision was made to ultimately slow the tempo of the combat down a little. All vehicles have a reduced top speed, and health and damage amounts were adjusted so that it ultimately takes longer to destroy an opponent. The gameplay, however, remains fast-paced and keeps its energetic atmosphere.

[h3]Content Changes[/h3]
Two vehicles were added to the second playtest: the Wagon XII and the T86 III. Both of these vehicles were in the original game and have slightly reworked models to bring about gameplay and aesthetic changes. These vehicles will require you to accumulate some of the game's new currency, Coins, in order to unlock; however, the prices have been significantly reduced for testing purposes and should both be easily purchasable after one game (so long as you play the game to the end). The game still features only one map, Greenfield Village, but this map has been reworked to fill in some of the open space and provide denser regions to test urban combat. The map, however, remains as a whole a very exposed battlefield.

[h3]Other Changes[/h3]
Extra settings were added, allowing one to adjust basic graphics settings and remap most of the input keys from the main menu. As the game now uses a P2P interface, a lobby system has been added where the host can adjust numerous settings in the game and configure each team. Some effects were added or modified to provide more relevant gameplay information and give a more immersive feel.


Please note that bugs are present in the game, and some issues are to be expected. I am aware of several small issues, but there is a possibility that the game will completely break at an inopportune time. If you encounter any bugs or issues while playing, please let me know. I will try to correct any major issues as soon as possible if any show up.

I currently plan to start creating mass amounts of tanks, maps, and game modes for this project in the near future. If all things go as planned, the third playtest (date unknown) will have mass amounts of content and will be presentable as an "Early Access" version of the game. However, what the content will look like depends heavily on the gameplay, which must be grounded before content creation can begin. Making content is one of my least enjoyed elements of game development, and before I begin grinding out this extended process, I need to know that the game is enjoyable and whether the process is worth grinding out. Your feedback is invaluable to the development of this project. Please reach out to me with any comments or suggestions concerning the game; if you don't know how to get in touch with me, you can use the Community Hub portal for the playtest to post any feedback. Furthermore, if you know anyone who would be interested in playing this demo, please reach out as I would greatly appreciate more testers for this game.

Thank you very much for your interest in the project! The playtest is planned to remain running until the next playtest releases; if you need a guide on how to play the game, please see the announcement for the first playtest. Once again, your participation is invaluable and very much appreciated, and I look forward to hearing your thoughts.

-Josh_007

notes.title: First Playtest is Live
notes.notes:
Good evening everyone,

The first test for [i]Steel Skirmish Reloaded: Online Multiplayer Tank Shooter[/i] is now live. I apologize for the extended wait for this demo, but I trust that you will not be disappointed. The game, in its current state, is certainly a long distance from full release, but enough content should be present to give an accurate evaluation of the final product's gameplay and atmosphere.

The game presently has three vehicles, all of which are available to you immediately, and one test map that will not be present in the final game. I am presently using a cloud-hosted server to run the game, but please note that only one match can be run on the server at a time. If you try to play while somebody else is using the server, you will not be able to connect to the server. Up to 20 players can connect to a match at once, and I encourage you to gather as many people in a single match as you can so that the gameplay and the server performance can be most accurately evaluated. Note that the server will wait ten seconds after the most recent connection before it starts the match, so if you are playing with others be sure to coordinate.

Note that there currently is no tutorial explaining controls and mechanics within the game client. Please refer below for a detailed summary.

[h3]Controls[/h3]
[list]
[*]Move: WASD
[*]Fire: LMB
[*]Zoom/sniper mode: RMB (hold)
[*]Activate sniper mode: RMB (hold) + Mouse scroll up
[*]Deactivate sniper mode: RMB (hold) + Mouse scroll down
[*]Boost: Left Shift (hold)
[*]Activate Powerup: Spacebar
[*]Handbrake: X
[*]Show team score: Tab (hold)
[*]Show expanded map: M (hold)
[*]Open menu: Escape
[/list]
[h3]Game Rules/Mechanics[/h3]
[list]
[*]Allied vehicles are always visible to you. Enemy vehicles will be visible on your client when they reach a specific distance to you or one of your allies. Enemies become highlighted when they are hit or take damage.
[*]Shell velocity is "infinite"; all shots hit their targets instantly.
[*]Each tank's gun has a limited range from which it can hit targets. Shots fired at targets beyond a vehicle's range will hit nothing. Refer to the stats in the pre-battle screen to see each vehicle's range.
[*]If a shot hits an enemy tank, one of two outcomes will occur, based on where the shell hits. If a region of spaced armor is impacted, no damage will be dealt. If the shot hits the enemy anywhere else, a fixed amount of damage is dealt and the enemy is launched in the direction of the shot. Bonus damage can be dealt if the enemy takes a strong impact as a result of the shot. Note that allies cannot be damaged by shooting them.
[*]The location where the gun is currently aiming is shown on the UI by a small dot. You can find the distance to this location directly below the dot. This indicator changes color based upon where the gun is currently aiming: green means a successful hit to an enemy, red means spaced armor, white means an obstacle or terrain, and gray means that the target is out of range.
[*]Two types of dynamic objects are scattered around the map: boulders and explosive barrels. Boulders serve as movable cover that can be destroyed by shots or impact. Explosive barrels will begin to burn upon shooting or strong impact and will explode shortly afterward. Upon explosion, they deal heavy damage to all vehicles near them.
[*]If you get destroyed in a match, you will be able to respawn up to three times. Once you get destroyed for the fourth time, you will be left to spectate.
[*]Only the Standard Match game mode is available in the current demo. In order to obtain victory under this scenario, a team must either eliminate all enemy players (destroy all enemy players four times so that none can respawn) or destroy the base by the team's spawn point.
[/list]

Once you are finished playing the demo, I highly encourage you to send me feedback. You can do this by any means, but if you're not sure where to drop any comments then please send a comment in the discussion board.

I will probably leave the playtest open for a couple weeks so that everyone who is interested has the opportunity to play the game. When and what the next playtest will be depends on feedback and on how much I am able to create in the coming months.

I cannot thank you enough for your interest in this project. I simply cannot continue development until I get your input on how the game plays and what you think of the concept. If you have any questions, comments, or concerns, please reach out to me via Steam or by other means.

-Josh_007
